title: Fallback lattice with time-bound rollforward and variant quarantine for pinned models
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers can pin to a specific model version for compatibility guarantees. When that pinned variant becomes unavailable (capacity, model deprecation, or incompatibility), we need a deterministic, auditable fallback policy that balances: 1) preserving pinned contract guarantees, 2) keeping customer traffic healthy (avoid long outages), and 3) minimizing silent quality regressions.

Scope: Implement a policy engine and runtime guards that (a) build a fallback lattice (region-aware + variant-aware), (b) apply time-bound rollforwards with TTL and quarantine windows, (c) support soft-deprecation notifications and automatic compatibility checks before rerouting, and (d) provide telemetry and API-level explanations for routed fallbacks. This ticket covers design, runtime changes for routing decision, rollout automation, and dashboards/alerts.

Out of scope: full UI in Console (a follow-up PM ticket will add a Console view), deep model-quality A/B evaluation harness (we expose hooks for future eval runs).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can compute a fallback lattice for a pinned version that includes regional variants and compatible model variants (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.1.x compatible pool)
Fallbacks are time-bound: an automatic rollforward only takes place after configurable TTL and is reversible within a quarantine window
Rollforwards require compatibility checks (signature, tokenizer, structured-output schema) before traffic moves to a variant
Operator/tenant-visible event is emitted whenever a fallback decision occurs, including reason, selected variant, and whether it was automatic or manual
Dashboards surface fallback rate, average time-to-rollforward, and number of quarantined variants; alerts trigger when fallback rate > 1% for 10m for customers with pinned versions
E2E tests cover regional failover, capacity-based fallback, and soft-deprecation-triggered rollforward scenarios
Feature flagging exists to enable/disable automatic rollforward per customer and default is off for enterprise tenants
design_notes:
Core concepts:
- Lattice model: nodes = (region, model-version, variant-type). Edges represent allowed promotion paths. Preference order: same-region compatible variant -> same-region newer patch -> cross-region same-variant -> cross-region compatible variant.
- Time-bound rollforward: To avoid silent regressions, an automated rollforward requires (1) TTL elapsed since initial failure, (2) successful lightweight compatibility checks (model schema, tokenizer smoke tests), and (3) health checks (latency, error rate) for the target variant.
- Quarantine: After automatic rollforward, the chosen variant enters a quarantine window during which we monitor quality signals and can auto-revert if thresholds exceed. Quarantine acts as a soft probation rather than permanent retargeting.
- Blacklist/whitelist guards: Maintain per-customer and global blocklists (e.g., known-broken weights).
- Explanation API: Every routed request can optionally include an explanation header/metadata with fallback reason and chosen endpoint id.
- Determinism & audit: Decisions are deterministic given the same inputs (region, tenant, pin) and are logged to the audit stream for replay.
- Config surface: TTL, quarantine window, fallback order, and drivers for compatibility checks are per-tenant configurable via API or defaults from the Console.

Trade-offs considered:
- Immediate rollforward reduces downtime but increases risk of quality regression. We counter this with TTL + quarantine and compatibility checks.
- Strict lock reduces customer disruptions but increases outage windows. We expose per-tenant controls so customers can choose their preference.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag gated behind runtime toggle + per-tenant opt-in.
2) Internal canary: enable for 3 internal tenants (dev+staging+prod-sandbox) and run for 48h. Monitor fallback telemetry.
3) Gradual external rollout: opt-in beta for selected customers with support package.
4) Default mode: automatic rollforward OFF; expose Console toggle (follow-up).
5) After 30 days of beta and stability checks, enable for tenants that choose 'auto-rollforward' in their settings.

Rollback: toggle off the flag and allow the system to resume strict pining; revert any active rollforwards using recorded audit logs.
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit the following metrics and events: fallback_attempt_total, fallback_success_total, auto_rollforward_count, quarantine_reverts, fallback_latency_ms. Events include: fallback_decision (with fields: tenant, original_pin, selected_variant, reason, deterministic_path). Dashboards: per-tenant fallback rate, median time-to-rollforward, rollback_count. Alerts: P0 if fallback_rate > 1% for any tenant for 10m, or quarantine_reverts > 5 in 1h. Logs to audit stream for forensic analysis.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for lattice generation and comparator functions. Integration tests in staging that simulate: regional outage (blackhole region), variant incompatibility (mismatched tokenizer), and deprecation lifecycle transition. Chaos test: induce transient failures at 1% sampling and ensure TTL + quarantine behave as designed. Load test to verify decision latency < 2ms added to routing path.

E2E acceptance harness: scriptable scenarios that assert both behavior and emitted events (audit + metrics).
